$comment: Spec pins for the design-conformance functional-acceptance suite (cinatra#985). Each entry pins the EXACT generated conformance manifest this repo verified against: `manifestSha256` is the sha256 of the committed manifest bytes under manifests/, `specContentHash` is the manifest's embedded spec-source hash (must match the manifest's own contentHash field). `source: "repo"` = pre-publication REPO-PIN fallback: the suite reads the committed manifest copy (verbatim generated bytes from the design-system source of truth, never hand-edited). Once the docs wave publishes the manifests under publishedBaseUrl, flip `source` to "published" — NO code change: the suite then ALSO fetches the published manifest and asserts its bytes hash to `manifestSha256` (upstream drift = a distinct, actionable red). To adopt a new upstream manifest version: replace the file under manifests/ with the regenerated artifact and update both hashes in the same commit.

manifests.$specCommit: design@6183a023fe6d185d64ad0d159a968da0ec3d9a6b — specs/app-components.html, the artifact pinned by cinatra#1544 on 2026-07-14 (the spec bytes at that commit hash to specContentHash and the generated artifact hashes to manifestSha256). DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED by the lifecycle-b W1 re-pin, and this note is the record of what moving it now costs. Upstream has regenerated this artifact FOUR times since this pin was taken — at design@ab19f01dafd1d123ed2963aec5d09300af1bf22c, design@5b8cdd04cf4698bc927984fe627b5ebc67ae8b6c, design@88dbdae8e8481643fd054aa8dd52acd4c1cc556f and design@fe2182547d4a98125a0968824ffb0d45fb25a8e5, each with different bytes and a different embedded contentHash, because the spec source moved under it each time. TWO of those four changed what the artifact DECLARES, which is what a driver has to answer: the first (design#85, 2026-07-17) ADDED the `breadcrumb-entity-resolution` surface, taking the count from two to three; the last (design#132, 2026-08-25) REPLACED `scheduling-trigger-tab` with `scheduling-step-configured`: the same section redrawn as the CONFIGURED READING of the standard scheduling step, so its actions become `save-schedule -> rearmed` and `cancel-schedule -> stopped` where they were `cancel -> cancelled` and `release -> released`, and it gains a `loading` state. The upstream artifact at design@fe2182547d4a98125a0968824ffb0d45fb25a8e5 hashes to 52615494243bb89764809afd8c8b8033b4722c0a1d1b6726452787973b490ecd and embeds contentHash sha256:617b86b316e3835c385ebb86e10ba250c6db03c486d3d0b9eccfcdcb780a476c. ADOPTING IT IS A SLICE, NOT A RE-PIN, and the three things it needs are named here so the next reader does not have to rediscover them. (1) `scheduling-trigger-tab` — its driver in conformance/contract.ts and its harness mount in src/app/design-fixtures/conformance/approvals-scheduling-fixtures.tsx drive `cancel` and `release` against a persistent Trigger tab that this drawing no longer has anywhere. That driver id is RETIRED WITH THE ADOPTION AND NOT BEFORE IT: the artifact pinned above still declares the surface, and a declared surface with no driver and no allowlist entry is a red, so retiring it first would break the suite to record a fact this note records without breaking anything. (2) `scheduling-step-configured` — its two actions have no counterpart to drive until the schedule step itself draws Save changes and the recurring-only Cancel schedule. (3) `breadcrumb-entity-resolution` — it has no driver, no harness mount and no testid-contract entry anywhere in this repo, and allowlist.json is shrink-only and may not gain entries, so it cannot be exempted and must be covered in the same commit that moves this pin. Until all three land, this pin names the artifact this repo actually verified against, which is the whole point of pinning one.
